subject: PII handling confirmation for prompts/outputs - Sunnyside Health
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@sunnysidehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: PII handling and retention (post-call recap)

Hi Jane -

Thanks again for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on Sunnyside's PII requirements and how Redwood can support them. Please correct me if I missed anything.

Summary of ask from your team:
- Confirm what types of data will be sent to the API (PHI/SSNs/names/free-text clinical notes).
- Ensure prompts/outputs are not used for model training and limit retention.
- Logging/audit evidence for SOC2 review (request for architecture diagram and sample logs).
- Data residency in us-east-1 and customer-managed KMS for encryption keys.

Redwood's current confirmation (hosted API):
- Prompts & outputs: by default, short-term retention for debugging and quality is 30 days. This includes full prompt text and generated outputs.
- Training: customer data (prompts/outputs) is NOT used to train or improve publicly released Redwood models unless explicitly opted in via a written agreement.
- Logging & metadata: request/response metadata (timestamps, route, model variant, token counts) retained up to 90 days by default; can be reduced by contract for enterprise customers.
- KV cache & ephemeral state: session-level KVs are ephemeral and not persisted as long-term customer records unless you enable a persistent store.
- Data residency: Hosted can pin data to a region (us-east-1 or eu-west-1) depending on plan; Dedicated/Private deployments provide exclusive residency in your VPC/region.
- Encryption: data is encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest; we support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated/Private.

Options we discussed to meet Sunnyside requirements:
1) Hosted + Contract Addendum: Disable retention of prompts/outputs (zero retention) and limit metadata retention; Redwood will provide written confirmation and an SLA/contract clause.
2) Dedicated/Private deployment: No prompts/outputs leave your VPC (recommended for highest assurance). You can provision CMK and control retention policies.

Next steps
- Jane: confirm whether Sunnyside needs zero retention or if 30-day short-term retention (with contract assurances) is acceptable.
- Rishi/Marissa: we will attach the SOC2 summary and the PII dataflow diagram for your security team.
- Neha: looping you for a quick look and to provide the SOC2 artifact and a signed statement template.

Attachments: redwood-pii-dataflow.pdf, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Thanks - I can jump on a short call with your security lead if that helps.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@sunnysidehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Thomas Lee <tlee@sunnysidehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RE: Follow-up: PII handling and retention (post-call recap)

Thanks Rishi - this is helpful. A few clarifying questions from our security and legal teams:

1) Can you confirm in writing that prompts/outputs will not be used for model training under our account unless we opt in? We need a sentence we can include in the DPA.
2) For the "30-day" retention: is that configurable per-account? If we request zero retention, what is the path and timeline to get that enforced?
3) For logs/metadata: can you provide an example redacted log sample and the current retention policy table (we need values for request payload retention, full response retention, and audit logs)?
4) Data residency: we require that all PHI stays in us-east-1. Do you support per-account regional pinning for hosted service or would this require Dedicated?

We also need a short written confirmation that Redwood will not surface PII in aggregate analytics or training datasets and that you have controls to prevent that.

If useful, I'll share a short list of contract language we typically request.

Thanks,
Jane
Security Ops Manager
Sunnyside Health
jane.doe@sunnysidehealth.com

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@sunnysidehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RE: Follow-up: PII handling and retention (post-call recap)

Hi Jane - great questions. See inline confirmations below; happy to put any of this into DPA language and sign a clause.

1) Training: Confirmed in writing: "Redwood will NOT use Sunnyside Health customer prompts, responses, or other customer-provided content to train, improve, or evaluate Redwood's public models unless Sunnyside Health explicitly opts in via a written agreement." We can add this sentence to the DPA.

2) 30-day retention: This is our default for hosted customers to allow debugging and quality work. It is configurable for enterprise customers. Path for zero retention: sign a minimal addendum (we'll attach a template) and we will disable storage of request/response bodies for your account within 3 business days after request + execution of the addendum. If you need immediate zero-retention from day one, Dedicated/Private is the recommended route.

3) Logs/metadata retention: Current defaults (hosted):
- Full request payloads (prompts): retained 30 days
- Full response payloads (outputs): retained 30 days
- Request/response metadata (timestamps, model, token counts): retained 90 days
- Audit logs (auth events, admin actions): retained 1 year by default (can be reduced)
We will provide a redacted sample log and the retention table in the attachment (see redwood-soc2-summary.pdf). If you want reduced retention (e.g., 7 or 0 days), we can commit to that by contract.

4) Data residency: Hosted can pin to us-east-1 for your account. For full isolation (no cross-tenant access), Dedicated/Private is recommended. We'll note your requirement for "PHI stays in us-east-1" and can provide a signed statement and architecture diagram.

Additional controls:
- Encryption: TLS in transit; AES-256 at rest. Dedicated/Private supports customer-managed KMS keys.
- Access controls: RBAC, SCIM for provisioning, and admin audit trails.
- Data minimization: we offer SDK-level redaction helpers and filters to remove sensitive fields before sending.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, redwood-pii-dataflow.pdf

Next steps
- I'll attach a short addendum template for zero-retention and a DPA clause so legal can review.
- Neha / Marissa: can you confirm routing the SOC2 artifacts and a signed letter template we can provide to Sunnyside?

Jane - let me know if you want to jump on a 20-min call with Neha (security) to walk through the SOC2 artifacts.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
